phase3_findings.anchor: the comment above sbl_build in the #1618/#1897 block; mirrored in lib/test/modules/coverage-map.json under keys 'scripts/skill-body-load-probe-verdict.py' and '1618'
phase3_findings.description: The diff-added comment states the universal 'Every child spawned below carries NO_COLOR/PYTHON_COLORS', and the two coverage-map notes mirror it as 'Every child the block spawns neutralises terminal colour'. The AC8 re-derivation assertion spawns a bare `git -C "$LIB/.." show 668a7899...:skills/review/SKILL.md` with no such prefix, and that child's output IS selection-determining — it becomes the on-disk control file read_controls compares the delivered body against. Orchestrator-confirmed against HEAD at lib/test/run.sh:25300.
phase3_findings.impact: No live fail-open. `git show <commit>:<path>` emits raw blob bytes with no colouring, and its output is redirected to a file rather than a terminal, so no escape sequence can reach the control file; a corrupted capture would fail the assertion closed in any case. The cost is a coupled comment/coverage-map trio that misdescribes what the block enforces, which a maintainer adding the next child would read as an already-enforced invariant.
phase3_findings.remedy: Scope the claim in all three copies to what is enforced (e.g. 'every helper and fixture-builder child below'), or add the prefix to the git invocation so the universal becomes true.

phase3_findings.anchor: assert_eq "#1618/#1897 skill-body: that reason no longer names the SKILL.md file path"
phase3_findings.description: The absent-string half of the boundary_dir reason pair is entailed by the present half. The preceding assertion pins that the reason contains `directory ('skills/review')`; this one asserts, from a second fixture build and a second helper spawn of the identical fixture with the identical repo-relative --root, that it does NOT contain `directory ('skills/review/SKILL.md')`. The helper emits exactly one `directory (%r)` occurrence per root from a single operand, and the asserted-present literal terminates in `')`, so it mechanically excludes the asserted-absent one.
phase3_findings.impact: The assertion can never go RED while its pair is GREEN, so it buys no discriminating power over the operand change it is meant to pin, at the cost of an extra fixture build and helper spawn. Against this repo's fewer-tests-by-default preference.
phase3_findings.remedy: Drop the absent-form assertion, or re-target it at a shape the present-form assertion does not entail.

defect_signature.location: lib/test/run.sh, "#1618/#1897 skill-body: that reason no longer names the SKILL.md file path"
defect_signature.claim: The absence assertion is entailed by the paired presence assertion over the same deterministic capture, so it can never fail independently.

phase3_findings.anchor: assert_eq "#1618/#1897 skill-body: the $_sbl_order fixture records both Skill loads", inside the for _sbl_order loop
phase3_findings.description: The two contains_name_* positive controls guard a positive-expectation assertion. Each order pays a second fixture build and helper spawn to assert `recorded Skill tool_use pairs: 2`. A positive control earns its cost when the assertion it backs is a NEGATIVE expectation a broken fixture or crashed helper would satisfy — as with late_body, whose main assertion expects 0. Here the main assertion expects 2 delivered-whole verdicts, which already goes RED for any fixture that failed to record both loads.
phase3_findings.impact: Diagnostic messaging rather than coverage; doubles this loop's process count.
phase3_findings.remedy: Optional — drop the two controls, or keep them explicitly as diagnostics rather than as coverage.
